items.t: Said too many NATO allies could not be relied on to support U.S. operations against Iran.
items.q: far too many of our NATO allies showed that they could not be relied upon to support our nation’s operations against Iran

items.t: Said military recruiting is having its strongest performance in three decades.
items.q: We are in the midst of a historic resurgence in military recruiting, with the strongest performance in three decades

items.t: Said the objectives of the Iran operations were to destroy Iran's missile stockpiles, launchers and defense industrial base, destroy its navy, and permanently deny Iran nuclear weapons (2026).
items.q: One, destroy their missile stockpiles, their missile launchers, and their defense industrial base — missiles and their ability to make them. Two, destroy their navy. And three, permanently deny Iran nuclear weapons forever.

items.t: Said cutting general and flag officer positions "is not a slash-and-burn exercise" meant to punish officers.
items.q: This is not a slash-and-burn exercise meant to punish high-ranking officers

items.t: Said the military must "act urgently to revive the warrior ethos" and rebuild the military.
items.q: The time for preparation is over — we must act urgently to revive the warrior ethos, rebuild our military

items.t: Said that Ukraine returning to its pre-2014 borders and joining NATO are unrealistic (2025).
items.q: Ukraine returning to pre-2014 borders, joining NATO are ‘unrealistic,’ Hegseth says

items.t: Said women should not have combat roles in the military (2024).
items.q: I’m straight up just saying we should not have women in combat roles.

items.t: Said that not acting would have been negligent, defending the Trump administration's decision to kill Iranian general Qassem Soleimani (2020).
items.q: Imagine if he hadn't acted," Hegseth said Friday while co-hosting "The Five." "The amount of negligence -- he'd be charged with knowing about the gathering threat and not stepping in.

items.t: Said troops with gender dysphoria have 30 days to leave military service voluntarily, stating 'TRANS is out at the DOD'.
items.q: Pete Hegseth says troops with gender dysphoria have 30 days to leave service voluntarily: ‘TRANS is out at the DOD’

items.t: Said "border security is national security" and that the department is prioritizing it.
items.q: Border security is national security – and we are prioritizing accordingly

items.t: Said civilian tenure at the military academies leads to "academic stagnation" and dilutes their focus on lethality.
items.q: we must address the structural mechanisms that have allowed civilian academic norms to dilute our focus on lethality

record.t: Signed a memo authorizing D.C. National Guard use of up to 60 marked patrol cars, tactical vehicles, boats and light towers in support of the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful mission.
record.q: Hegseth signed an Oct. 29 memo authorizing up to 60 marked patrol cars, Humvees, military tactical vehicles, D.C. National Guard boats and up to 20 light towers and generators

record.t: Announced plans for the first new U.S. military base in about 40 years during his "State of the Force" address at Marine Corps Base Quantico.
record.q: We haven’t built a new base in this country in 40 years. That ends now

record.t: Signed a memo approving cuts to the military's joint pool of general and flag officer positions, with some jobs downgraded to colonel and Navy captain level.
record.q: In a Sept. 16 memo approving reductions to the military's joint pool, Hegseth directed officials to establish O-6 requirements for general and flag officer positions identified for downgrade

record.t: Testified before the Senate Armed Services Committee on the Department's budget request, including funding for the Golden Dome missile defense system and the F-47 fighter.
record.q: makes generational investments in the President’s priorities, including developing the Golden Dome for America

record.t: Asked Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George to step down and retire effective immediately.
record.q: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has asked the chief of staff of the Army, Gen. Randy George, to step down and retire effective immediately.

record.t: Ended the appointment of civilian employees to tenured faculty positions at the U.S. military academies.
record.q: The United States will no longer appoint civilian employees to tenured positions at United States military academies

record.t: Announced a letter of acceptance for a Qatari Emiri Air Force facility at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho.
record.q: Today, we’re announcing a letter of acceptance in building a Qatari Emiri Air Force facility at the Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho

record.t: Was authorized by President Trump's Executive Order 14347 to use the secondary title "Secretary of War."
record.q: The Secretary of Defense is authorized the use of this additional secondary title — the Secretary of War

record.t: Announced that the American soldiers honored for their actions near Wounded Knee in 1890 would keep their Medals of Honor.
record.q: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced on Thursday that American soldiers honored after their actions in 1890 near Wounded Knee should be recognized as heroes and keep their Medals of Honor

record.t: Testified before the House Armed Services Committee that the Pentagon keeps plans "for any contingency" when asked about Greenland and Panama.
record.q: Our job at the Defense Department is to have plans for any contingency

record.t: Ordered senior Pentagon leaders to draft plans for annual 8% cuts to the defense budget, with border operations, nuclear modernization and missile defense exempt, according to a memo reported by the New York Post.
record.q: demanded a proposal that would include annual 8% cuts to the Pentagon’s roughly $850 billion budget

record.t: Signed a memorandum to rename Fort Liberty in North Carolina to Fort Bragg.
record.q: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a memorandum on Monday to rename Fort Liberty in North Carolina to Fort Bragg.

record.t: Was confirmed by the Senate as Secretary of Defense by a vote of 51-50, with Vice President JD Vance casting the tie-breaking vote.
record.q: issued the following statement after the Senate confirmed Pete Hegseth to be Secretary of the U.S. Department of Defense (DOD), by a vote of 51-50, with Vice President JD Vance casting the tie-breaking vote

record.t: Canceled former Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Mark Milley's security detail and clearance and directed the Pentagon's acting inspector general to launch an investigation into whether he should be demoted in rank.
record.q: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has canceled former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Mark Milley’s security detail and clearance — and directed the Pentagon’s acting inspector general to launch an investigation into whether the retired soldier should be demoted in rank
